document.title: Scene-Setter for the Visit of Senators Levin and Warner (Islamabad 06322)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), "No-Go" Tribal Areas Became Basis for Afghan Insurgency Documents Show
document.note: [Secret] Prepares Senators Levin and Warner for their Pakistan visit. Pakistan's cooperation against al-Qaida and the Taliban has been unstinting, and Musharraf has held firm by placing five Islamist leaders under house arrest and changing military leadership (ISI's Mahmoud replaced by Ehsan ul Haq). Sanctions are lifted and aid is rising, but Pakistan remains wary of the Northern Alliance and wants Kabul demilitarized under UN or OIC control.

mentions.quote: PRESIDENT PERVEZ MUSHARRAF AND HIS TEAM WILL UNDOUBTEDLY WANT TO DISCUSS THE POLITICAL FUTURE OF AFGHANISTAN
THE GOP ABANDONED THE TALIBAN AND SO CRACKED DOWN ON THEIR DOMESTIC SUPPORTERS IN PAKISTAN
MUSHARRAF WOULD LIKE TO SEE A "BROAD-BASED," MULTIETHNIC COALITION INSTALLED IN KABUL

key_claims: Pakistan abandoned the Taliban and cracked down on domestic supporters after Musharraf backed the war on terrorism.
Pakistan's earlier Taliban support was driven by the need for strategic depth against India.
Musharraf fears the Northern Alliance is hostile to Pakistan and wants a broad-based, multiethnic government with a substantial Pushtoon element.
Pakistan wants Kabul demilitarized under UN or OIC control.
Pakistan faces domestic religious-party opposition; Islamist leaders were placed under house arrest.
US aid to Pakistan increased sharply, with sanctions waived and a USD 600 million support agreement signed 15 Nov 2001.
